title: Activepieces vs Celigo: Pricing & Features (2026)
summary: Activepieces vs Celigo offers a choice between self-hosted automation and a managed platform with built-in finance and ecommerce system integration.
body_markdown:
## Pricing compared: what Celigo and open-source automation cost


**Maintenance has a price** , and the two tools show it differently.


One vendor publishes its plans starting at free ($0, with 1,000 credits a month), with unlimited flows on every plan, while Celigo quotes every tier through sales, so you can only compare a published number with an estimate.


On the same five measures, the table sets both side by side.


What to take from it: the open-source vendor tells you the cost of growth up front, from $0 on Free to $200 a month flat on Team and from $36,000 a year for Embed, and with Celigo you learn it in a sales call.


Activepieces Celigo


Pricing model Tiered plans: Free, Plus, Team, Embed Sales-quoted, all tiers


Billing unit Plan with users and monthly credits Set in your quote


Entry price Plus $16/mo annual; Team $166/mo annual; Embed from $36k/yr Quoted by sales


Growth effect Move up a published tier Renegotiated per quote


Free tier Free plan None published


### Activepieces plans and entry price


[$192 a year](https://www.activepieces.com/pricing) buys Plus, and Team is $1,992, so a small team can start for less than one month of many enterprise tools.


Monthly credits climb with each plan. The Free plan gives 5 users 1,000 credits, Plus gives 5 users 10,000, and Team gives 25 users 50,000, so upgrading to Plus multiplies per-user capacity tenfold. Moving up buys fifty times the free allowance.


A credit is the unit of metered usage: work your flows do draws credits down, and the allowance resets each month.


Running steps and calling AI features are what consume them, so a long flow or an AI-heavy one costs more per run than a short one.


As a rough guide, a simple flow with a trigger and a few steps that spends a handful of credits per run would get you a few hundred runs from the Free allowance, which suits a pilot but not a busy storefront.


Check the pricing page for exactly how each action is counted before you size a plan.


Embed is the tier for putting the builder inside your own product. It adds the right to offer automation to your customers under your branding, which the other plans are not priced for, and its terms are sales-quoted.


Billed monthly, Plus cloud is $20 and Team cloud is $200, which means you're choosing between $240 and $2,400 annually. A self-host server runs about $6.70 a month, meaning about $80 per year. With ops time counted it comes to $121.


**That's above Plus cloud, so self-hosting pays only if you need control of the infrastructure, not to save money.**


You will not find a Celigo tier price published, and its billing unit is unpublished too: what you are charged for is set in your quote.


The comparison chart puts Activepieces' entry at[$7,200 a year](https://www.activepieces.com/pricing) , against $10,000 for Workato and $24,000 each for Boomi and MuleSoft.


Treat that as a starting estimate, since your quote depends on scope.


- Comparing a quoted price with a list price and calling the gap savings.
- Leaving ops time out of a self-hosted figure, which turns $6.70 into $121.
- Pricing today's connections, not the ones you'll add in two years.
